note:
ISO 2026-W43 runs from October 19 through October 25. Uranus is about 4.7° in ecliptic longitude from Aldebaran in Taurus.

**Naked eye:** No principal lunar phase is listed this week. Check the Moon's position each night and favor darker hours for low-contrast targets. Use Tiaki, Fomalhaut as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -10.2; direct motion; 53.2% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Saturn in ecliptic longitude Oct 24 13:05 UTC. Conjunction with Neptune in ecliptic longitude Oct 23 23:54 UTC. Conjunction with Pluto in ecliptic longitude Oct 19 07:49 UTC. Mercury: Naked eye; magnitude 0.1; direct motion; 46.6% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Station Oct 24 07:12 UTC: turns retrograde. Jupiter: Naked eye; magnitude -1.9; direct motion; 99.3% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Saturn: Naked eye; magnitude 0.4; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Oct 24 13:05 UTC. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.6; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Neptune: Telescope; magnitude 7.7; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Oct 23 23:54 UTC. Pluto: Substantial telescope; magnitude 14.6; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Oct 19 07:49 UTC.

**Binoculars:** Trace the charted figure of Oct, then identify β Oct at its plotted position.

**Small telescope:** Deer Lick Group: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Cave Nebula: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.

story_candidates.dek: Deer Lick Group is an observing target in Pegasus carried by the weekly Calendar.
story_candidates.body:
Why it is here: The Calendar selected Deer Lick Group as one of this week’s fixed-sky observing targets.

How to find it: Trace the preserved Pegasus stick figure from its brighter labeled stars, then identify the target on the corresponding charted segment.

story_candidates.dek: Tiaki is a star in Gru of catalogue visual magnitude 2.07; its declination determines which latitudes can observe it.
story_candidates.body:
The stored catalogue gives a visual magnitude of 2.07. This is a catalogue value, not a prediction of its brightness this week. Lower magnitudes mean brighter objects; sky brightness and altitude affect whether you can see the star.

Its catalogue position is approximately right ascension 22h 42m and declination -46.9°. These reference coordinates describe its sky location; they are not an observing time or a current altitude.

At the almanac’s default latitude of 45° N, this star does not rise above the geometric horizon. These are geometric calculations from declination, excluding refraction and local obstructions. Darkness and the time of culmination must still be checked for the observing date and your location.

How to find it: Establish the preserved Gru constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.

Sources: Star Almanack’s stored fixed-object and expanded Bayer catalogues; accepted constellation figures and guiding-star routes. Visibility limits are original geometric calculations from catalogue declination, not weekly predictions.
